*Below is a transcription of a message left in a sealed cache and found at a Durmand Priory dig site in Janthir Gravis. We discovered it had been something of a make-shift staging ground for an individual named Doyen Sidony to coordinate military movements across the northern Janthir isles. —Historian Meliza*  

Brother,  

I have left this for you in the event that I do not return from the upcoming engagement with the shadowstalkers. The mursaat, as you well know, are a cunning sort. Even with the potential depths of our power, we withhold. Anything drastic could upend Tyria's balance, even stir another cycle. We must be wise.  

You have your own tasks, and I pray to the elders that you return to our smiling faces upon completion. Should you not, I only ask that you take leave of Janthir expeditiously. Do not hold onto any foolish notions of vengeance. They will hunt you down and pry whatever they so desire from you. Your survival comes first and must always come first.  

It is my duty as the eldest to say such things. We've already lost our Lasia, and I'll not lose you if I can help it.  

Until the next,  
Meliore

We met them at the pass in Thunderhead Peaks: five thousand of our finest soldiers blocking the only way forward for the Stone Summit forces. We were outnumbered, yes, but the narrow pass would force them to fight on our terms, and our archers controlled the cliff faces. It was our best opportunity to stop their advance.  
  
Had it been only the traitors, we'd have surely prevailed; their first wave crashed weakly into our shields and were cut down by our support from above. Then the mursaat appeared. I've seen many things in my day, but the horrors they inflicted on our forces will haunt me to my dying breath. Within minutes of their assault our lines broke, soldiers trampling each other as they fled. The mursaat killed most of us as we fled. But after what I saw that day, I think they might have been the lucky ones.

Hey, Commander!

Sorry for sending this antiquated note, but while I was working with Yao and Joon, communications became critically important to solving their power problems. The good news is, we made some serious upgrades to the comms systems I developed. The bad news is, I can't just patch the system. I have to roll this out to every user individually...AND you won't be on the upgraded network until you get the update. Hence, the mail. I've attached a one-time-use service chip that'll apply the update to your comms unit automatically. Once you perform the update, you won't need to do anything...but feel free to test it out. Everyone else should have theirs already...this tech is still experimental, so you may run into some glitches if you overextend the system.

Taimi

PS: Ivan's been calling me every five minutes, complaining that he has something important, yadda yadda yadda... Maybe ask him what he needs, so he stops bugging me while I'm trying to work? Okay, gotta go... BYE!

My esteemed and devoted Priest Elkan,

I'm at my wit's end. If life as the old mentor monk means putting up with young Panco one day longer, forget it! He stinks, overeats, only pretends to pray, and yesterday made fun of my eyebrows because they meet in the middle. I was explaining my theory of what might exist beneath the Harvest Temple, when he slapped me on the forehead and said, "Sorry, my mistake. I thought your eyebrow was a giant, hairy caterpillar."

Honestly, THIS is the next generation of monk that's supposed to guide us through the dark years ahead?

Please, for the love of the gods, send better candidates! Ones who would be genuinely interested in hearing that, based on my reading, I believe ley lines intersect deep beneath the Harvest Temple, making it a truly magical place! And possibly why it's been the center of so much destruction in the past, with the Jade Wind, the Affliction, the Void...

...And, dare I say it, Panco!

Seriously, please help.

Your humble servant,
Mulof

Dear Arch Researcher Tunsi,  
  
In celebration of the 99th anniversary of your natal egress, we are pleased to present you with a pineapple upside-down cake. Thank you for exhausting these last several decades of your life in pursuit of rigorous science and relentless innovation!  
  
If you wish, you may let your staff eat cake during any downtime between experiments. Calculated from the prior decade's health examination logs, your odds of continued survival beyond the age of 100 diminish exponentially, so please enjoy this opportunity for rest and relaxation. In the words of our late Arch Headmaster Quag, "Science never stops, so naturally, then, neither can we." 
  
As a reminder to staff, be sure to sign below to claim 20 minutes of cake time. This will ensure your compensation reductions are appropriately prorated.

Arch Researcher Tunsi

*Foreword by Researcher Hui*

They say that believing in the gods "fell out of fashion" following the Zhaitan Disaster. While true in some—arguably most—cases, belief in the "human" deities continues to prosper quite prominently in underprivileged communities. My own grandparents (who have long since passed) were both fervent followers of Dwayna. Although they were both survivors of the Zhaitan Disaster, neither ever abandoned their belief.

Even when pressed with uncontested proof of Soo-Won's existence and thought "benevolence," they chose to worship the old. The familiar.

In the face of trying events such as the Zhaitan Disaster, I can imagine why some would hold on to what is known. We all do that in times of great strife. In this book, I will be interviewing individuals from all over Cantha in an effort to compile a general understanding of belief in the empire, examine its relationship to trauma, and hypothesize why many still believe in the gods of old.

Foreword:

It is a rather common delusion that we built the city of Ahdashim. However, I have never been nor will be a common djinn, for I possess not only the attunement of air, but also an infinite intellect and a voracious appetite for academia.

Many of my years have been consumed by our shared history in my quest for the secrets of our world. So, for your benefit and mine, I have scribed this 565th edition historical tome detailing the rise of the Original Four and their connection with the lifeblood of Ahdashim.

We have always been bound to Ahdashim. Long before we harnessed it, Ahdashim suckled from the ley line upon which it perched. For years, the city bent the elements to its will and thus protected the natural world from all tyranny and evil.

Until, that is, four of our most powerful ancestors discovered a way to channel it themselves. After converging with the ley line, the Original Four displayed ethereal elementalism to become the first guardians...the Cardinals of Ahdashim.

While my ancestors delved into the earth for supremacy, my years buried in our scriptures have  granted me something far more wondrous.
